chapter: Old New Orleans bands and Buddy Bolden
title: Sound of the early bands, blues and Bolden's powerful cornet
summary: Tio says early bands played straighter with less variation than today, played blues and waltzes and quadrilles, and that Bolden was a powerful cornetist.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Is there any band you can think of that would sound or any music you can think of that would sound something like that music then? I mean was it was it a different sound then to some of these jazz bands they have now? Or would it be about the same?

Well, it would be say the bands today use a little more variation than they did in that particular day. Because they use more variation than they did in those days. They played mostly a lot of straights but some variations.
Did they play what they call blues? They played the blues quite a bit?

Yeah, they had the blues all right. They had modern blues but they didn't have blues like they got them today. Some blues, I can't think of the name of them but they're blues all right. They were blues.
In better words, blues was kind of common. You played blues in the days. It was common stuff. You tell your all real. That's a blues band. They played the blues.
But this Bowling band didn't only play the blues. They played the Wilds and Quadros and something?
Oh yeah. Yeah. They had a good band to play that. They had a good band. It wasn't a dollar part of that. They had a good band.
I always hear Bowling as being a very good cornet player in the sense that he was a powerful cornet player.
